notable_absence.finding: The --default option's own three-value enum is internally inconsistent with its own OPTIONS text: the option's accepted values are documented as '"admins", "ro_admins", or "none"', but two sentences later the same paragraph says 'If this option is set to "roadmins" then all SASL users...' - switching from the value ro_admins to roadmins (matching the --roadmins FLAG name, not the --default value it just declared). A reader following the stated enum literally and passing --default ro_admins would, per the page's own inconsistent wording, be unclear whether that is even the documented value. This is a same-page internal contradiction, not just a drift from an external catalogue.

cross_component_finding: This page's RBAC framing is exactly the terminology drift this round is watching for: it grants 'administrator privileges' and 'read-only administrator privileges' to SASL users via --admins/--roadmins, but never once uses the registry's own internal role names (`admin`, `ro_admin`) or roles.md's exact display labels ('Full Admin'/'Full Administrator', 'Read-Only Admin') - the phrasing is generic prose, not a role citation tied to the 56-role catalogue. Separately, the SEE ALSO section links to '[admin-role-manage](couchbase-cli-user-manage.md)' - the link TEXT names a command called 'admin-role-manage', which does not exist anywhere in this batch or the couchbase-cli suite; the link TARGET is user-manage.md. This is either a stale/renamed command reference or a copy-paste error in the link label, and it sits directly beside a second, correctly-labelled '[user-manage](couchbase-cli-user-manage.md)' link pointing at the exact same target - meaning the SEE ALSO section has a working duplicate link and a mislabelled duplicate link to the same page, with no way for a reader to tell whether 'admin-role-manage' was meant to be a real, different subcommand.
